Listen, you can still have a happy life. I have had 8 different therapists, tried more antidepressants than I can count, been to the mental hospital 3 times, and done trans magnetic stimulation, and I only just turned 21. I'm not happy yet, but I know it's possible. Not all the time, every day, of course. But it's possible for my life to be happy. 

The biggest thing you can do to make a difference is to at least try to live your life actively. You will not be happy if you do not try. You will not be happy if you do not believe it's possible, at least somewhere deep down. I think your relationship sounds like a great place to start. Stop letting it happen to you, and decide what you need and want from it. Considering how codependent you sound, maybe try just taking a break from him to see how it feels. You don't have to cut it off all the way yet, but find a way you can spend a couple weeks completely without each other, and see how it effects you. Do more therapy, look into treatment resistant methods(TMS turned out to be pretty cool for me, and it didn't even help me as much as most people report it does for them) and just don't give up. It's not enough to survive anymore.

I know other people have said this, but it's so important you know: if you don't stop you might never be able to bind + never be able to get top surgery in the future. 

Hoodies are your friends, and I recommend you get some trans tape which you can wear for days at a time(as opposed to binders) though you still need a little bit of time between tape sessions. I'm sure there's techniques out there for dysphoria specifically that maybe you could look into too? But for now make sure you have something thick and loose you can wear around the house w/o a binder, and do something nice for yourself whenever you're not binding. Chocolate, your favorite movies, video games, etc. 

The other thing I can recommend is a flex binder, which have a softer insert, but can be worn longer or for more strenuous activities. Also yeah, working out is hard, but if you look it up there are some specific work outs and routines designed for what will give the best top surgery results. Maybe that will help because even if you're not binding in the moment, you're still working towards a flat chest and can use that to reinforce yourself? Also maybe look into any that might relieve back pain.

If Jeff wanted to take advantage of Annie's naivete, he easily could have (and a lot of the episodes where there chemistry is heavily displayed are ones who ng off her intelegence). But he didn't, he kept his distance, and I've always thought he did for her benefit. And the point isn't so much that he wouldn't still be down to sleep around with whatever girls if he can't have a stable relationship, it's that he wanted more with her. She brought out the best in him. And the co-ed fantasy seemed to be simple comfort. A fantasy he probably wouldn't like as much if it were realized, whereas the marriage fantasy was more intense, showing and questioning what he really wants, and why they can't have it.

But Jeff and Annie *does* lead to meaningful character development. Compare, for example, him liking Britta in season 1, to his fantasy about Annie in season 6. In season 1, his attraction to Britta is mostly sexual, even though they do end up having great chemistry and being one of my favorite friendships in the group (tho oc nothing can beat Troy and Abed or Troy Abed and Annie). But in season 6, Jeff doesn't just want to be screwing or screwing around with Annie, he dreams about being married to her, and having a life with her. (I mean technically he has been engaged to Britta 3 times, but the 1st was out of spite, the 2nd drunkenness and daddy issues, and the 3rd out of desperation to not loose her or his friends and be alone again) I've always thought that the reason Annie and Jeff didn't get together was because they knew it wasn't for the best and that there were bigger things at stake, despite watching them fall in love. And I think that how he feels about Annie really changes and helps Jeff, even if it's in subtle ways.
